age.long_description: Age group of the texter as recorded by Crisis Text Line ('<14' is CTL's '13 or younger'). 'Overall' covers all conversations, including the large majority with no age recorded. Conversations with no age recorded are not published as their own group.

ctl_pct_{variant}.short_name: Crisis Text Line: % of conversations about {variant.short_name}
ctl_pct_{variant}.long_name: Percent of tagged Crisis Text Line conversations about {variant.short_name}
ctl_pct_{variant}.short_description: Percent of Crisis Text Line conversations with at least one issue tag that were tagged {variant.short_name}, by quarter.
ctl_pct_{variant}.long_description: Quarterly number of Crisis Text Line text/chat conversations tagged {variant.short_name}, divided by the number of conversations with at least one issue tag recorded, times 100, rounded to 0.1. A conversation can carry several tags and is counted once in each, so topic percentages overlap and add up to more than 100. The denominator includes conversations tagged only with topics not published here (e.g. Racism, School). 'Abuse' combines CTL's emotional, physical, sexual and unspecified abuse tags. Counts are suppressed before the percent is calculated: a specific state-by-age cell is suppressed if its topic count is below 4, and any cell is suppressed if a state or national total (all ages and/or all states) is below 25 or the tagged-conversation denominator is below 25. Additional cells are suppressed where a suppressed value could otherwise be recalculated (complementary suppression, GaussSuppression R package). True zeros are never suppressed and are published as 0. Suppressed values are NA with ctl_pct_{variant}_suppressed = 1. A value is NA with the flag 0 when there were no tagged conversations in that cell (the percent is undefined). Age is recorded for only about 4-7% of conversations (varies by year), so age-specific values describe a small subset of texters; state is recorded for about 78%. Age was almost never recorded from December 2019 to March 2020, so most age-specific cells in 2020 Q1 are missing. National ('00') and 'Overall' age values include conversations with no reported state or age. CTL's tagging practices changed over time; notably, the share tagged Suicide fell through 2023 and rose sharply in 2024 Q2 in every state and age group, which likely reflects a change in tagging rather than a change in need.
ctl_pct_{variant}.statement: In {location}, {value}% of tagged Crisis Text Line conversations in the quarter ending {time} were about {variant.short_name}.

ctl_pct_{variant}_suppressed.long_name: Suppression flag for percent of Crisis Text Line conversations about {variant.short_name}
ctl_pct_{variant}_suppressed.short_description: 1 if the {variant.short_name} percent was suppressed for privacy, 0 otherwise.
ctl_pct_{variant}_suppressed.long_description: Binary flag: 1 if Crisis Text Line suppressed the {variant.short_name} percent (because the topic count, a total, or the tagged-conversation denominator was too small to publish, or by complementary suppression); ctl_pct_{variant} is then NA. Suppressed values are not imputed. 0 = not suppressed. A value can be NA with this flag 0 when there were no tagged conversations in that cell.
ctl_pct_{variant}_suppressed.statement: In {location}, the suppression flag for {variant.short_name} is {value} (1 = suppressed).

ctl_crisistrends.name: Crisis Text Line Crisis Trends
ctl_crisistrends.description: Crisis Text Line is a nonprofit that provides free, 24/7, confidential text-based mental health support and crisis intervention in English and Spanish across the United States and Puerto Rico. Crisis Counselors tag each conversation with the issues discussed. CTL Data Engineering provides PopHIVE with de-identified conversation counts aggregated by month, state, age group and combination of issue tags. PopHIVE sums these to quarters, applies small-cell and complementary suppression (GaussSuppression R package), and publishes each topic's share of conversations with at least one issue tag, by state and age group, from July 2018 onward. Processing happens in a separate PopHIVE repository; only the suppressed percentages are published here. Note the data describe people who chose to contact Crisis Text Line, not the general population; age is recorded for only about 4-7% of conversations (almost none from December 2019 to March 2020) and state for about 78%; topic tags are applied by counselors, and tagging practices have changed over time. The numbers are not expected to match crisistrends.org exactly, because Crisis Trends includes conversations that are excluded from this dataset under data-sharing restrictions.
ctl_crisistrends.restrictions: Attribution to Crisis Text Line required. Cite as: Crisis Text Line (2026). Crisis Trends. https://crisistrends.org/ (data obtained via the PopHIVE platform).
